title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Timeline:
- 2025-11-02 09:12 PST: Alerts triggered from healthcheck for customer A private deployment. Multiple API requests failing with 502/504 from control plane -> managed nodes.
- 2025-11-02 09:27 PST: Verified node-level agent logs. Errors indicate DNS resolution failures for model artifact mirror (s3-compatible) and upstream telemetry endpoints.
- 2025-11-02 10:03 PST: Confirmed some nodes could reach mirror IPs, others could not. Hypothesis: partial routing / VPC peering route table issue or asymmetric egress via NAT.

Quick summary of symptoms (observed):
- Intermittent DNS timeouts (dig returned ; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> model-mirror.internal.example.com; ;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345)
- TLS handshake failures when connecting to internal artifact mirror from pods: "SSL_connect: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown" and occasionally cert verify failed (self signed) when using curl inside node.
- Some app containers get HTTP 502 from local proxy (envoy) with upstream connect failed; other containers on same node are fine.
- Traceroute from failing pod to mirror's IP stops at the VPC peering virtual interface (no replies).

Commands run / outputs (snippets):
- kubectl exec -it pod/worker-abc -- dig +trace model-mirror.internal.example.com ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

- nslookup from node (working node):
Server: 10.0.0.2
Address: 10.0.0.2#53
Name: model-mirror.internal.example.com
Address: 10.4.32.18

- nslookup from failing node:
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

- ip route show (on failing node):
10.0.0.0/16 via local dev0 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.34.12
169.254.169.254 via 10.0.34.1 dev eth0
default via 10.0.34.1 dev eth0
(note: no route for peer VPC CIDR 10.4.0.0/16)

- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-aaaa
  (noticed route table entries for peering not present on subnet rt)

- sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v (on node)
Chain POSTROUTING (policy ACCEPT 0 packets, 0 bytes)
  MASQUERADE  all  --  10.0.0.0/8        0.0.0.0/0
(However some subnets deliberately had NO NAT due to design; suspect egress inconsistencies)

- openssl s_client -connect 10.4.32.18:443 -servername model-mirror.internal.example.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735268349040:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol:ssl/ssl_lib.c:1905:

- curl -v https://model-mirror.internal.example.com/health** (from failing pod)
* Rebuilt URL to: https://model-mirror.internal.example.com/health
*   Trying 10.4.32.18...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.4.32.18 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to model-mirror.internal.example.com port 443: Connection timed out

What changed recently / likely causes:
- Route table for new subnets (net-new) created during onboarding had a different RT assoc. Looks like peering routes were never propagated to those RTs.
- Terraform apply for customer A (2025-10-28) included move of some subnets to 'private-no-nat' profile. That might have removed NAT gateway egress for nodes that still need to reach external model mirrors in another VPC (peered).
- TLS errors: mirror uses mutual TLS for some endpoints; some nodes had an OS-level CA bundle older than the issuer (we saw cert verification errors on older AMI).
- DNS: We use Route53 inbound endpoints for cross-account private hosted zones. Inconsistent security group rules on the resolver ENIs blocked UDP/53 from some subnets (SG allowed only from VPC CIDR, but our peered CIDR is different and SG didn't include it).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Missing route table entries for peering on affected subnets -> traffic to peered CIDR is routed to default gateway (no route), causing timeouts. Explains traceroute stopping at peering interface.
2) DNS resolver ENI SG blocking traffic from some subnets (UDP/53 and TCP/53) -> returns SERVFAIL or timeouts.
3) Egress NAT missing for 'private-no-nat' subnets where shards expect to reach external endpoints via NAT -> some flows fail.
4) OS CA bundle / TLS protocol mismatch on older AMIs causing cert verify failures or unsupported SSL protocols. This is secondary but explains the handful of TLS errors after connectivity restored.
5) Asymmetric routing: reply path blocked by NACLs on peered VPC -> intermittent reachability.

Immediate remediation steps performed (and result):
- Added explicit route for 10.4.0.0/16 -> pcx-0abcde on route tables of affected subnets (manual) at 2025-11-02 11:05 PST. Result: pods in those subnets now have direct route; some pods could reach mirror but DNS still failing for a subset.
- Updated security group on inbound resolver ENI to include peered CIDR (10.0.0.0/16) and specific subnet ranges 10.0.34.0/24 at 2025-11-02 11:22 PST. Result: DNS resolution improved for most nodes.
- Rebooted a couple of problematic nodes (old AMI) after updating CA bundle (2025-11-02 12:10 PST). Post-reboot, curl TLS verify succeeded for those nodes.
- For subnets intentionally created without NAT, we patched a subset of pods to use VPC endpoint for S3-compatible mirror (when available) and deployed a temporary NAT gateway as hotfix for others.

Open action items / next steps:
- Infra infra-team: audit Terraform module for subnet profile 'private-no-nat' and ensure peering route propagation is part of onboarding. (owner: Samir)
- SRE: Create automated route-table validation during deploys that checks peering routes for customer private deployments (owner: Eliot).
- Security: Confirm Route53 inbound resolver SG baseline includes peered CIDRs or use resolver endpoints per-az with proper SGs; document required SG rules. (owner: Maya)
- Release eng: Build AMI bake that includes up-to-date CA bundle and TLS ciphers we support, and a gossip to auto-drift detect older AMIs in fleets. (owner: Devops team)
- Product: Update onboarding checklist for customers with cross-account peering to include DNS inbound endpoint checks and explicit route verification.

Notes to self / troubleshooting breadcrumb log:
- If I see SERVFAIL in dig but node-level nslookup works -> likely resolver SG / ENI reachability problem.
- If traceroute drops at peering hop -> route table missing on source VPC or NACL blocking return path.
- For TLS handshake errors post-connect -> check openssl s_client output, CA bundle, and TLS protocol versions; older openssl on AMI may not support TLS1.3 handshake that mirror enforces.

Suggested permanent fixes (longer term):
- Add a Terraform check/plan hook that fails if peering routes are not referenced in newly created route tables for private deploys.
- Centralize CA bundle management via an SSM parameter and ensure AMI bake pulls latest truststore at boot.
- Make Route53 resolver SG baseline part of the customer VPC module with explicit tagged security group applied to inbound endpoints.
- Add synthetic monitors from each customer subnet to model mirrors / internal infra to detect routing/DNS issues earlier.

People to ping: Maya Chen (networking), Samir Patel (infra), Eliot Brooks (SRE), Leah Wong (customer success lead for customer A).

References / tickets:
- NET-4233 (primary incident ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/187 (temporary route addition + docs)
- Slack thread: #infra-private-deploy-thread-2025-11-02 (contains packet captures)

Next quick tests to run if issue reappears:
- from failing pod: curl --resolve model-mirror.internal.example.com:443:10.4.32.18 https://model-mirror.internal.example.com/health -v --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt
- tcpdump on resolver ENI: tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53 and capture for 60s, look for UDP vs TCP and source IPs
- check aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters tag:Name=route53-resolver-enid

Last thought: this one was largely human/config drift (new subnet profile + incomplete terraform module assumptions). We should treat peering+DNS as an atomic checklist item for onboarding private deployments.

-- devon
summary: Debug notes for customer A private deployment networking incident: mixed DNS timeouts, missing peering routes, NAT/egress profile issues, and TLS CA mismatches. Immediate fixes included adding routes, adjusting resolver SG, and temporary NAT; longer-term fixes proposed (TF checks, AMI bake, resolver SG baseline).
